purpose: R34 production-EFFECTIVE-BATCH topology (Codex R33-review): the R32/R33 reference dump had every rank independently build the loader (which replicates); the REAL reference trainer train_pytorch_new.py builds the loader on rank 0 only and fans out SUCCESSIVE micro-batches to each rank. This measures the reference's actual fanout topology and states RLinf's, then records the fix.

reference_fanout.trainer: scripts/train_pytorch_new.py: rank-0-only loader (line 866); each step rank 0 pulls world_size*gradient_accumulate successive next(data_iter) micro-batches and fans one block to each rank (lines 952-961).
reference_fanout.measured_by: tests/unit_tests/_ref_fanout_dump.py (single-process mirror of rank 0: loader at per-rank batch 32, pull world_size=8 successive micro-batches/step, hash every frame).
reference_fanout.conclusion: RANK-DISJOINT -- the reference production EFFECTIVE per-step batch is 256 (world_size 8 * per-rank 32), confirmed (256 unique frames/global step).

rlinf_topology.worker: rlinf/workers/sft/fsdp_vla_sft_worker.py builds a loader PER RANK via build_behavior_sft_dataloader(cfg, world_size, rank, ...).
rlinf_topology.pre_fix: RANK-REPLICATED (effective batch 32) -- BehaviorSftDataset._select_streaming_chunk read torch.distributed, but the DataLoader workers are SPAWNED (fresh interpreters that do not inherit torch.distributed) so they read rank=0 -> every rank replicated rank 0's chunks (R32 dump: nw=8 -> 32 unique/step; nw=0 control -> 256).
rlinf_topology.config_intent: actor.global_batch_size=256 = micro 32 * 8 ranks; the rank-replication collapsed the effective batch to 32 (1/8 the configured value).

root_cause: The reference production trains at EFFECTIVE batch 256 (rank-disjoint fanout) while RLinf trained at EFFECTIVE batch 32 (rank-replicated, spawn workers lose the dist rank) -- an 8x effective-batch difference, the likely driver of the r22-vs-r24 gap (RLinf at batch 32 sees 8x fewer unique frames/step and descends faster to 0.046 vs the reference's batch-256 0.090). This corrects the R33 verdict that BOTH were effective batch 32 (that read only the loader helper, not the trainer's rank-0 fanout).
fix: Thread explicit rank/world_size: build_behavior_sft_dataloader passes its rank/world_size into create_behavior_sft_data_loader -> BehaviorSftDataset (stored as _dist_rank/_dist_world_size); _select_streaming_chunk prefers the explicit values (falling back to torch.distributed only when not provided), so spawned workers partition by the correct per-rank id -> RANK-DISJOINT (effective batch 256, matching the config + the reference). fsdp_vla_sft_worker already passes self._world_size/self._rank, so the fix is wired into production with no worker change.
next: Confirm the fix by re-dumping RLinf at the 8-rank/num_workers=8 topology with the explicit-rank path -> RLinf now rank-disjoint (256). The FINAL task15 validation is the 8-GPU first-50 rerun under the fix (effective batch 256) -- expected to descend like the reference (~0.090); task15 closes only if the original 50/50 DEC-1(b) gate passes or an accepted plan evolution.

fix_confirmed.method: re-ran the 8-rank/num_workers=8 RLinf topology dump with the fix (tools/_loader_topology_dump.py _build_rlinf now passes dist_rank=rank/dist_world_size=world, mirroring the production worker).
fix_confirmed.verdict: RANK-DISJOINT — after the fix RLinf emits 256 unique frames per global step (was 32 before), i.e. effective batch 256, matching the reference + the configured global_batch_size=256.
